references.name: Francis Galton
references.desc: Hereditary Genius (1869) — first scientific study on origins of high achievement; Darwin's cousin

references.name: Charles Darwin
references.desc: Responded to Galton that "zeal and hard work" matter more than innate ability

references.name: William James
references.desc: "The Energies of Men" (1907) — argued most people use only a fraction of their potential

references.name: Martin Seligman
references.desc: Duckworth's advisor; pioneer of Positive Psychology and learned helplessness research

references.name: Dan Chambliss
references.desc: Sociologist who studied competitive swimmers for six years; showed excellence is mundane — not magical

references.name: Anders Ericsson
references.desc: Deliberate practice research; expertise requires ~10,000 hours of purposeful, structured practice

references.name: Carol Dweck
references.desc: Growth mindset vs. fixed mindset — believing abilities can be developed through effort

references.name: Catharine Cox
references.desc: Stanford study (1926) cataloguing 301 eminent historical figures; persistence mattered more than IQ

references.name: Gabriele Oettingen
references.desc: Showed positive fantasizing without planning backfires; developed WOOP goal-setting framework

references.name: Amy Chua
references.desc: "Tiger Mom" — argued loving what you do isn't enough without working hard at it

references.name: Jean Cote
references.desc: Sports psychologist; showed early sampling across multiple sports produces better long-term athletes

references.name: Barry Schwartz
references.desc: The Paradox of Choice; compared career discovery to finding a romantic partner

references.name: Malcolm Gladwell
references.desc: Popularized the 10,000-hour rule; critiqued Enron's "talent mindset" culture

references.name: Jeff Bezos
references.desc: Left finance to start Amazon; exemplifies passion + perseverance over safe career paths

references.name: Pete Carroll
references.desc: Seattle Seahawks coach; rebuilt philosophy around John Wooden's principles after being fired

references.name: John Wooden
references.desc: Legendary UCLA basketball coach; model of purpose-driven coaching that Carroll studied
